Wallace, C.D. (2021). Utilizing renewable hydrogen for fuel-cell mine haul vehicles in Canada: a techno-economic assessment. Research project for the MSc in Sustainable Energy Development, University of Calgary, Calgary, Alberta, August 2021.

Capstone techno-economic model of one 290 t Komatsu 930E: diesel base case versus fuel-cell electric truck with PEM-electrolyzer hydrogen, 20-year fictitious Ontario mine. Loaded: Table 4.1 (diesel, 2020/2030/2050), Table 5.1 (FCEV, three years), Table 5.2 (electrolyzer, three years), LCOH by scenario (Fig. 22 labels and text), efficiencies from Fig. 6 labels, derived GJ/h and OPEX (2 % of CAPEX). Not loaded: cost-stack figures (Figs 15-19), appendix tables, wind farm costs, carbon tax, policy results; per-tonne values are in _other-values because ore throughput is printed ambiguously (5.22 "tons/day/truck"). Locator: printed page numbers (PDF page = printed + 10). Traps: all costs CAD with no price year stated (2020 used = investment start); 2030 and 2050 values are author-assumed learning rates (-2 %/yr truck cost, +1 %/yr fuel efficiency), not forecasts; hydrogen use is sized by energy equivalence with diesel so the 36 % vs 50 % powertrain efficiency gain is not credited in the 2020 hydrogen rate; unit typos in Table 5.1 (fuel cell kWh, battery kW, replacement $/kWh); text 3,336 L/day vs calculated 3,366; Scenario 3 LCOH 2030 text 4.28 vs figure 4.24; 2030 diesel fuel cost marked as assumption.
